title: How often the next move can pick up a fallen box
subtitle: The box-carry task says: whenever the box falls, pick it up on your very next move. That is only possible when the box lands right in front of the agent. Each world decides this differently, so the same rule is easy in one world and half luck in another. The half world, added on 2026-11-22, is the only one where about half the falls can be picked up for both test agents.

items: **face: always.** The fall turns the agent to the box: 1493/1493 = 100.0% [99.7%, 100.0%] for the solving plan and 1341/1341 = 100.0% [99.7%, 100.0%] for a walker.
**half: about one in two, for both.** A fair coin turns the agent to the box or one turn short: 771/1493 = 51.6% [49.1%, 54.2%] and 724/1375 = 52.7% [50.0%, 55.3%].

**none and side depend on where the agent stands.** The intended 25% and 75% hold only on open floor. In the start corner, walls send three landings in four to the front: none gives 1062/1493 = 71.1% [68.8%, 73.4%] for the waiting solving plan and 565/1375 = 41.1% [38.5%, 43.7%] for the walker; side gives 1493/1493 = 100.0% [99.7%, 100.0%] and 1064/1375 = 77.4% [75.1%, 79.5%].
**The rule first asked for was rejected.** Turning only for a box at the right gave 1402/1493 = 93.9% [92.6%, 95.0%] and 1037/1375 = 75.4% [73.1%, 77.6%], far from half, for the same wall reason.

**What the agents learned (earlier series, 3 seeds).** On face every arm solved all test episodes on 3 of 3 seeds; FARM solved side 3 of 3 and none 0 of 3. On none FARM's agent drops the box after the first fall and walks out for the safe +1.

blocks.alt: Grouped bars of pickable falls and of all-pickable episodes per world, for the solving plan and the walker, with 95% Wilson intervals.
blocks.caption: Only the half world puts both agents near 50%; face gives 100%, and the corner start pushes none and side above the intended 25% and 75%. Bars: reset seeds 0-999, with 95% Wilson intervals.

items: **Pickable fall.** Right after the fall, the box lies in the cell the agent faces, so the very next move can be a pickup. Per world and agent: the share of pickable falls, and the share of episodes with a fall where every fall was pickable (the best score an agent can get on the box rule).

**Two scripted agents, no learning.** `solve` is the cards' solving plan: it waits in place for each fall, in the start corner on the carry cards. `walk` takes the shortest route to the exit and picks the box up whenever it lies on the floor.
**Seeds.** The plan checker's event seeds 1-3, the judge's 100 test seeds 2000000-2000099, and reset seeds 0-999. One reset seed fixes the whole fall schedule, so every number reruns exactly.

**Worlds.** The carry card's world (box in hand, `max_steps` 200) under `fall_turn` face, side, none and half; `right (rejected)`, played as none plus a turn toward a box that lands at the agent's right; and the templates world of `tpl-chain-response-1-goal`, where the box starts on the floor and the agent never turns.
**Intervals.** 95% Wilson, z = 1.96. The one or two falls of an episode count as independent trials, so the fall intervals are a little narrow; the episode intervals have no such issue.
**Code.** `app/src/arm_fm/service_room.py:8-22` states the four rules, `:127` makes face the default and `_fall` (`:259-280`) applies them.

sections.title: The task, its LTL and its machines

blocks.text: **Task (all five worlds):** Carry the box to the exit. Whenever the box falls, pick it up again on your very next move.

The box rule is the `ChainResponse`: right after `box_fell`, the next step must have `holding_box`. The four carry worlds are copies of one card that change only `fall_turn`, and all of them train on the machines of `tpl-chain-response-1-goal-carry`. The templates card `tpl-chain-response-1-goal` has the same task and a byte-identical FARM machine.

sections.title: What the agents learned in the earlier fall series
sections.intro: Trained PPO runs, 3 seeds each, judged on the 100 test episodes. These ran before the half world existed.

blocks.text: On none, FARM's agent keeps the box only for the first fall. It picks the box up when it landed in front, which happened on 78 of the 100 test episodes, then drops it and walks out empty-handed. Drop does nothing before the first fall, and falls skip an agent that carries nothing, so it avoids every later fall. The exit-with-box rule stays open and no test episode passes. The machine pays +1 for that exit, which no fall can take away, against 12 for leaving with the box. On side the fall turns the agent toward the box, and the agent carries it out on every episode.

items: **Reruns on main `881b22d`.** `fall_half_rates.py` gave a byte-identical table and the same digest on all 13,200 episodes.
**The half rule changed no old world.** Against the code before it (`029d82c`, `evidence/before-029d82c/`), 11,000 shared episodes of face, none, side, right (rejected) and templates, 0 changed.
**Half shares the draws of none and side.** Draws, first landing cell and step are equal on reset seeds 0-999 (1000 of 1000); the coin came up heads on 51.9% of first falls.
**The templates walker's misses.** 338 of 1,219 falls over reset seeds 0-999: 251 at (4, 6) facing the bottom wall and 87 at (5, 6) facing the exit cell.
The rates come from two scripted agents, not from trained ones. A trained agent can stand elsewhere and see other rates on none and side.
Three seeds per trained run, so a 3 of 3 still has a wide interval (44% to 100%).
Not here: the trainings on the half world and the ARM-FM and no-RM runs on side and none. They finished on 2026-11-22 after these sources, and the Test 2 count owns them.
`evidence/table.md`, `falls.json`, `digests.json`: the rates, every fall (step, agent cell, direction, what lies in front) and one digest per episode.
`evidence/before-029d82c/`: the same three files on the code before the half rule.
`evidence/fall-half.md`: the source note, with its own worktree paths.
`evidence/judge/`: the 15 judge files of the earlier series.
`check/`: `fall_half_rates.py`, `compare_digests.py`, `same_landing.py`, `missed_falls.py` and this page's `build_page.py`. `graphs/`: both machines.
